name: Back-Face Culling for Ray Casting
aliases: Two-Pass Raycasting with Back-Face Depth Buffering
Two-Pass Raycasting with Backface Entry/Exit Points
definition: An optimization technique to determine the entry and exit points of a ray into a volume by rendering the back faces of the bounding cube to a texture, avoiding the need to compute ray-cube intersection analytically.
summary: Back-face culling for ray casting is a two-pass optimization that uses GPU rasterization to determine ray entry and exit points, avoiding analytical intersection calculations.
